## Attachment A to Document 58

## OUTSIDE CONTRACTING CHECKLIST

This checklist for UAW-GM locations has been developed and approved by the National Parties to be used in conjunction with the Advance Discussion Procedure for all instances where the use of an outside contractor is contemplated for work that is of a normal and historic nature to the skilled trades bargaining unit. Prior to awarding a contract to an outside contractor for Skilled Maintenance, Tool, Die, Weld Tool work, this check list is to be used.

The checklist should be used as a tool to ensure that relevant factors related to the subcontracting provisions of the National Agreement are fully considered prior to a contract being awarded. The National Parties reserve the right to amend this checklist.

<table border=1><tr><td colspan="2">ADVANCE NOTIFICATION PROCEDURE</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>Please place a “+” in the “Fully Considered” column after each factor is considered.(See Paragraph 183(c)(d)(e), Appendix F, F-1, Documents #58, 59, 98, 100)</td><td>Fully Considered</td></tr><tr><td>1)</td><td>Provide the Union with written advance notification prior to awarding a contract (except where time and circumstances prevent it.)</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>a)</td><td>Describe in detail all relevant information pertaining to the work in question</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>b)</td><td>Has the work in question normally and historically been performed by bargaining unit employees?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>c)</td><td>Has the affected skilled trade(s) been identified?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>d)</td><td>Have the other required resources been identified?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>e)</td><td>Has a timeline for the project been established and reviewed in detail?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>f)</td><td>Have all the relevant best practices developed and approved by the UAW Document 138 task teams been reviewed?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>g)</td><td>Has a detailed explanation been given to why the services of an outside contractor are being contemplated?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>2)</td><td>Satisfy the conditions and limitations related to the Louis G. Seaton Letter dated December 14, 1967. (Appendix F and Doc. #58, National Agreement)</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>a)</td><td>Are there any special skills involved?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>b)</td><td>Are specialized tools, equipment or facilities required that are not available?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>c)</td><td>Have all rental or lease options been considered?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>d)</td><td>Are specialized contractors required?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>i)</td><td>If yes, identify the reason(s)</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>e)</td><td>Does the projected plant bargaining unit workload preclude the possibility of completing the work within the time limits set forth by Management.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>f)</td><td>Can the plant bargaining unit employees be competitive in cost and quality in the performance of this work?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>g)</td><td>Are there other competitive challenges facing the plant and its employees, such as a change in production schedules, model changes or plant rearrangement?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>3)</td><td>Can portions of the project be pulled ahead or individual job assignments adjusted to accommodate the completion of the work in question?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>a)</td><td>If yes, identify that portion in detail.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>4)</td><td>Indicate the contractors projected manpower and work schedule including extended daily and weekend hours, if any.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>5)</td><td>Identify any plant skilled trades employees on layoff or on Protected Status that may be utilized.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>6)</td><td>Notify the union if a warranty has been provided in association with the purchase or lease of machinery and/or equipment and indicate the length of the warranty (normal and/or extended) being provided.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>7)</td><td>Identify what the warranty includes.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>8)</td><td>Identify who will perform the warranty work (e.g., OEM, 3rd party, etc.).</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>9)</td><td>Will any training be required after warranty expiration?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>a)</td><td>If yes, identify the training plan, timeline and how training will be provided.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>10)</td><td>If a service contract is contemplated, consider the service contract proposal in the same manner as contracts for the performance of skilled maintenance work normally and historically performed by represented skilled trades&#x27; employees.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>11)</td><td>Are there any proprietary agreements associated with the work?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>a)</td><td>If yes, provide a detailed explanation (including the duration).</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>b)</td><td>Have other non-proprietary alternatives been explored?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>c)</td><td>Identify who will perform the proprietary work (e.g., OEM, 3rd party, etc.).</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>d)</td><td>Will any training be required if the proprietary agreement expires?</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>i)</td><td>If yes, identify the training plan, timeline and how training will be provided.</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>12)</td><td>Consider the Union&#x27;s comments in light of all attendant circumstances and give appropriate weight to those comments.</td><td></td></tr></table>
